# Phase A grounding: forwarding a failing CI check to the owning worker

Repo: kapetan-io/dispatch (Go). Everything below was read from the code in this checkout
(paths relative to repo root) and from docs/design/decision-log.md, docs/design/blueprint.md,
docs/guide.md, docs/config.md. Line numbers are approximate. Nothing here was run against a
live GitHub: this sandbox has no `gh`/network check, so GitHub API schema claims are marked UNVERIFIED.

## Objective (approved by the user, not up for discussion)

When a check fails on the pull request of an In Progress or In Review ticket, the dispatcher
types one message into that ticket's worker, once per failing check run, so the worker fixes it
without the user relaying anything. Workers never poll GitHub. Decide whether this extends the
existing pull request nudge or becomes its own rule, and what the dispatcher's cache must
remember so a failure is forwarded once.

## 1. The tick and the purity boundary

`dispatch.go tick()` runs: read Linear tickets, herdr snapshot, treehouse leases -> `workers`
map -> `readPRs` -> `reconcile.Plan(input)` (pure, no side effects; dry run prints its actions)
-> `settle(cache, ...)` rolls the cache forward -> the executor loop acts on each Action
(Nudge calls `herdr.Prompt(pane, text)` and mutates the cache entry on success only) -> cache saved.
Order matters and is documented in settle's comment: Plan reads LAST tick's cache; settle runs
BEFORE the actions; the executor then adds (Nudges++) or undoes. A refused nudge ("herdr refuses
a worker that turned blocked after the snapshot") is not counted and is retried next tick.
CLAUDE.md: new code is Go, tested through the surface (tests call `dispatch.Run` with fake
`gh`/herdr/linear binaries via a `harness`; see review_test.go `prState`, `h.pr(...)`, `h.prReads()`).

## 2. The existing PR nudge (what "extend" would extend)

- `internal/pullrequest.Read` makes ONE `gh api graphql` call per ticket: PR number, url,
  headRefOid, mergeable, reviewDecision, `commits(last:1){commit{statusCheckRollup{state}}}`,
  reviewThreads(first:100). It folds the rollup into an aggregate: `state FAILURE|ERROR` appends the
  string "a failed check" to `PR.Problems`; any state != SUCCESS clears `checksPassed`.
  There is NO per-check identity today: no check name, no id, no URL, no conclusion. The model
  cannot tell two failing runs apart or tell a re-run from the original.
- `PR.NeedsWork()` = any Problems. `PR.Problem()` joins them ("a failed check and a merge conflict").
- `reconcile.inReviewIdle` (reconcile.go): only for status In Review AND worker Idle. If
  `pr.Ready` and `cache.ReadyHead != pr.Head` -> Notify the user. If `pr.NeedsWork()` ->
  `Nudge{Reason: "PR needs work: <problem>", Text: PRNudge}`; PRNudge = "PR %s for %s has %s.
  Handle it as your build skill's step 7 says, and push." (text is fixed; build skill and tests rely on exact wording).
- It is count-based, not event-based: `cache.Entry.Nudges` increments on every send; at
  `nudge_limit` (default 2) -> Escalate to Needs Human with one comment. `NudgesAt(status, head)`
  returns 0 when the status or `PRHead` changed, so a push (head moves) resets the count. Same
  failing check, same head => the same nudge repeats once more, then escalates.
- `prRelaunch`: In Review ticket, PR NeedsWork, worker State None -> Plan emits Launch (a worker
  is relaunched on the existing tree), counted by `Entry.Relaunches` against nudge_limit; the nudge
  itself is sent the following tick once the new worker is idle. So a FAILED CHECK is currently
  also what relaunches a gone In Review worker.
- `Input.ReadsPR(t)`: only status In Review, not design/design-review, no children, labels not
  truncated, and worker state None or Idle. Working/blocked workers => no gh call ("cost nothing").
  An In Progress ticket's PR is NEVER read today. `readPRs` finds the PR by `t.Branch`
  (Linear branchName) in the repo clone `in.Repos[repoLabel]`; unread/failed reads are put in
  `PRReadFailed` and the ticket is absent from `PRs`.
- `settle` keeps `Entry.PRHead` only while In Review (clears it otherwise: "a stale one would hide
  a push later") and only updates it when the PR was read this tick.
- Escalation (`escalate()` in dispatch.go) resets Nudges and moves the ticket to Needs Human.

## 3. The comment nudge (the closest precedent for "its own rule")

Decision-log item 11 (settled 2026-10-09, ENG-257): "Dispatch is the event broker. ... Each tick
it polls those sources, compares what it finds with its cache, and forwards what the receiver
doesn't know yet, as a nudge ... Workers never poll. A new kind of event is a new forwarding
rule in the dispatcher, never an instruction for workers to check something themselves." The
comment nudge "is one such rule, like the PR nudge", and "counts toward neither the stall nor the
PR limit, and never escalates". The ready-for-review notify (ENG-256) is "the same idea pointed
at you".
Mechanics (reconcile.commentNudge, dispatch.go settle/PendingComments, cache.CommentSeen):
- Fires for In Progress OR In Review, worker Working or Idle (typing into a working Claude session
  delivers mid-turn); NOT Blocked (text would land in the question dialog; fires once unblocked);
  never for design / design-review labelled tickets; suppressed on the idle In Progress resume tick.
- Dedupe state is a single high-water mark `CommentSeen` (creation time string) per ticket. First
  sighting ("" -> "0"/newest) records without nudging, so restarting `dispatch run` nudges nobody.
- A mark is held back while a nudge is owed or the worker cannot take it: `PendingComments()` makes
  settle skip advancing it; the executor advances it only after `herdr.Prompt` succeeds. This is the
  pattern that makes delivery at-least-once and retries a refused prompt.
- It takes the tick ahead of stall and PR nudges (`watch` calls commentNudge first, returns
  after one action), so a ticket gets at most ONE Action per tick from `watch`.
- Absent-ticket handling in settle: a ticket missing from the Linear read keeps only
  LaunchFailures, PendingComment/TicketID, TeardownWarned; and `CommentSeen`/`ReadyHead` ONLY while
  it still holds a treehouse lease (so a surviving worker still hears, and a relaunched worker
  on a kept tree doesn't announce a head twice). Entries that become empty are deleted.

## 4. The cache

`internal/cache/cache.go`: `Cache map[string]Entry` (key = ticket identifier), JSON file, atomic
temp+rename write, corrupt file => empty cache. Header contract: "Deleting the cache loses little:
counters reset, a last-seen status may repeat one notification, a comment posted meanwhile gets no
nudge ..., and an escalation comment Linear has not yet accepted is never posted." Any new field
must keep that property (a lost cache may cost at most a repeated message, never a crash or a
silent stuck state). Current fields: LastStatus, LaunchFailures, Nudges, PRHead, Relaunches,
ResumePending, NotifyPending, ReadyHead, BlockedTicks, PendingComment, TicketID, CommentSeen,
TeardownWarned. One owner per concept; the entry is per TICKET (a ticket may hold leases in
several repos, but one PR/branch is read per ticket today via t.Branch).
Single dispatcher process holds a lock (`internal/lock`) for the tick, so the cache has one writer.

## 5. Worker side

skills/build/SKILL.md: "The dispatcher is the only clock, so run no /loop, cron or polling. A nudge
from the dispatcher is your wake-up, and its text comes from the user." Step 7 "Feedback until
merge" (decision-log): "A flaky check gets its own ticket and a re-run. A real failure gets fixed."
The PR nudge text says "Handle it as your build skill's step 7 says, and push" (changed from "Fix it
and push" so the worker still verifies the claim). A forwarded CI failure must keep that stance:
it is a claim to verify, not an order to patch. Nudges carry no source tag.

## 6. Constraints that fall out of the grounding

1. One gh call per ticket per tick today, via GraphQL, only for idle/gone In Review workers. The
   Objective needs In Progress PRs and (by the comment-nudge precedent) busy workers too. That
   widens ReadsPR and the per-tick gh cost (blueprint "Scale": "one gh api graphql call per In
   Review ticket whose worker is idle or gone"; "workers that are working or blocked cost no call").
2. The current read has no per-check identity. Forwarding "once per failing check run" requires
   the read to expose at least a stable per-run key. UNVERIFIED GitHub facts the design leans on:
   `statusCheckRollup.contexts` is a union of `CheckRun` (databaseId, name, conclusion, status,
   detailsUrl, completedAt) and `StatusContext` (context, state, targetUrl, createdAt); a re-run
   of a check/workflow creates a new CheckRun with a new id (so "run" identity changes on re-run);
   a legacy StatusContext has no id; contexts is paginated (`first:N` + `pageInfo.hasNextPage`,
   and the existing code errors rather than silently truncating, see maxThreads); the rollup
   `state` FAILURE|ERROR is the aggregate used today and which conclusions (CANCELLED, TIMED_OUT,
   STARTUP_FAILURE, ACTION_REQUIRED) count as "failing" is not decided anywhere in the repo.
3. Dedupe state must survive: a refused/failed prompt (retry next tick), a tick where the worker
   was Blocked (fire later), a tick where the PR read failed (don't lose or duplicate), a push
   (head moves; old runs belong to the old head), a re-run (new run id), and the worker being
   gone then relaunched. Memory must stay bounded (no unbounded growth of ids).
4. Two rules that both react to "a failed check" for the same ticket (PR nudge + CI forward)
   would send two messages for one failure and two escalation clocks. The design must leave
   exactly one owner of "a failed check" (red flags: split ownership, two ways to do one task).
5. `watch` yields at most one Action per ticket per tick; `Plan` and its dry run must stay pure.
   The Nudge executor branches on `Action.Reason` to decide which cache field to advance.
6. Relaunch of a gone In Review worker keys off `PR.NeedsWork()` (which includes "a failed check").
   If CI failures leave `Problems`, the relaunch trigger must be preserved some other way.
7. `PR.Ready` requires all checks SUCCESS; unaffected but shares the same parse.
8. Docs that describe today's behavior and would change: docs/guide.md "Nudges and notifications"
   (lines ~72-78) and "In Review", docs/config.md `nudge_limit`, docs/design/blueprint.md
   (acceptance criterion 9, Nudges section ~143, cache section ~276-289, Scale ~300),
   decision-log item 11.

## 7. Questions the design must answer (candidates: take a position and justify it)

- Extend the PR nudge or a separate rule? What happens to the "a failed check" problem string, the
  nudge_limit/escalation interaction, the relaunch path, and the PR-ready logic?
- What identifies "a failing check run" (key), and what exactly does the cache store, with what
  bound and what reset condition? What does cache deletion cost?
- One message per run, or one message per tick listing every newly failing run?
- Busy workers (Working) and Blocked workers: same policy as the comment nudge, or idle-only?
- What does the message say (fixed text, check name(s), URL), and does it preserve step 7's
  "verify the claim, flaky checks get a re-run"?
- How is the PR read widened (In Progress tickets, working workers, status contexts), and what
  is the added gh cost? How does a failed read behave?
- First sighting: after a fresh cache, is an already-failing run forwarded or only recorded?

# Forward a failing CI check to the worker that owns the PR (candidate 1)

## Problem

When a check fails on the PR of an In Progress or In Review ticket, the worker must be told once per failing run, without polling GitHub itself. Today "a failed check" is one string in `PR.Problems`, folded from `statusCheckRollup.state`. It has no run identity. It reaches only an idle In Review worker, through the PR nudge, which repeats on a count and escalates at `nudge_limit`. Five things the design has to respect: Plan stays pure; `watch` returns at most one Action per ticket per tick; the cache has one writer and losing it costs at most a repeated message; "a failed check" needs exactly one owner (grounding §6.4); and a gone In Review worker is relaunched today because of a red check (`prRelaunch` reads `NeedsWork()`).

**Premise check 1: "the failure belongs to the PR nudge."** Building this from scratch, with decision-log item 11 in hand ("A new kind of event is a new forwarding rule in the dispatcher"), the PR nudge would not own checks. It is a *state* reminder. It says "your PR still has problem P", repeats while P stands at one head, and counts toward escalation (`NudgesAt`). It runs only on idle In Review workers (`ReadsPR`, `inReviewIdle`). A check run is an *event*: it has an id, it finishes once, and a re-run is a different run (UNVERIFIED that the rollup keeps only the latest). The PR nudge also cannot express "once per run". Its text names no check, and its count resets on a push, not on a new run. The objective also needs In Progress and busy workers, and the PR nudge reaches neither. If "a failed check" stayed in `Problems`, an idle In Review worker would get the PR nudge and the CI forward for one failure, and there would be two escalation clocks. **Verdict: no.** Checks leave the PR nudge completely and become their own rule. That rule owns the forward, the relaunch trigger and the escalation backstop.

**Premise check 2: "a per-ticket counter or high-water mark is the right memory."** The comment nudge uses a mark (`CommentSeen`) because comment times only grow and an old comment never needs attention again. Neither holds for checks. `databaseId` order is start order, not finish order, so a slow job with a lower id that fails after a faster one would sit below the mark and never be forwarded. A legacy `StatusContext` has no id at all. A mark also cannot answer the question the backstop needs: "was the worker told about a run that is *still* red?" A counter cannot answer "which run" at all. From scratch, the memory is **the set of runs this worker was told about, scoped to the PR head and trimmed to what is still failing.** That set is bounded by what GitHub shows right now (≤ 100 contexts), never by history.

```go

type PR struct {
    Number int; URL, Head string
    Problems      []string // review-side only: changes requested, unresolved thread, merge conflict
    Failing       []Check  // finished checks on Head that did not pass
```

## Tradeoffs accepted

- We accept more gh calls (working workers, In Progress tickets) in exchange for a working worker hearing about red CI mid-turn, the way it already hears about comments.
- We accept one repeated message after cache loss, a return from Needs Human, or re-entry, in exchange for never staying silent about a red check. Recording on first sighting, as the comment nudge does, would make cache loss a stuck PR.
- We accept that a CI-only In Review ticket escalates on the first idle tick after a forward that the worker ignored, rather than after `nudge_limit`. This is deliberate. Step 7 leaves no legitimate way to sit idle on a red check: a fix means a push, and a flake means a re-run. `!ChecksRunning` covers the re-run window.
- We accept that `nudge_limit` now counts review rounds only. A CI fix loop is bounded by pushes and re-runs, not by a count.
- We accept that cancelled and action-required runs are forwarded even though the worker may not be able to act on them. The worker reads the conclusion and decides under step 7. An unknown conclusion is never silently dropped.

## Problem

A check that fails on a ticket's PR must reach the ticket's worker once per failing run, while the ticket is In Progress or In Review, whether the worker is working or idle, without the user relaying it. Today the only CI signal the dispatcher has is the rollup aggregate `statusCheckRollup.state`, folded into `PR.Problems` as the string "a failed check" (`internal/pullrequest/pullrequest.go:133-136`), consumed by `inReviewIdle` (idle In Review only, counted in `Nudges`, escalates at `nudge_limit`) and by `prRelaunch` (gone In Review worker). An In Progress PR is never read; a working worker's PR is never read (`ReadsPR`). Constraints the shape must honor: `Plan` stays pure and `watch` yields one Action per ticket per tick; the executor mutates the cache only after `herdr.Prompt` succeeds; `settle` runs before the executor and reads last tick's cache; deleting the cache may cost a repeated message but never a stuck state; exactly one owner of "a failed check"; the build skill's step 7 stance ("a claim to verify; flaky gets a re-run") and the fixed-text nudge convention.

**Premise check.** Three premises hide in "extend the PR nudge or its own rule":

1. *"The failure belongs to the PR nudge."* No. The PR nudge is a repetition clock for a stuck idle worker: `NudgesAt(status, head)` resets on a push, the escalation text is "stayed idle through N nudges about <PR> without pushing", and it fires only for `worker.Idle` on In Review. A CI failure is an event with identity (a run), the Objective says "once per run", and it must reach working workers and In Progress tickets, neither of which a counted clock should touch (counting a mid-fix working worker toward Needs Human is wrong). Decision-log 11 is explicit: "A new kind of event is a new forwarding rule in the dispatcher." Built from scratch with per-run identity available, "a failed check" would never have been a `Problems` entry; it is there because the rollup `state` was the only CI datum the read fetched, so the one rule that read PRs took it.
2. *"The dispatcher polls GitHub each tick."* Yes, this would exist: decision-log 11 settled that dispatch is the broker and workers never poll, and the build skill forbids workers from looping. What would not exist is today's read scope ("idle or gone In Review"), which was a cost rule derived from the single consumer. With an event rule, the right scope is "every ticket whose worker could take a message", and the cost is one `gh` call per live worker.
3. *"A per-ticket counter or mark is the right memory."* A counter is for a clock; a high-water mark (the comment nudge's `CommentSeen`) is for a totally ordered stream. Check runs are neither: several fail on one commit, a re-run is a new run with a new id, and completion order is not a reliable order of discovery. The right memory is a small set of run keys scoped to one head, which the head move already resets, the same signal `PRHead` already carries.

So: a separate forwarding rule (`ciNudge`) that becomes the only owner of failing checks. The PR nudge, the relaunch reason and `PR.Problems` lose "a failed check". `PR.Ready` keeps requiring the rollup to be SUCCESS (unchanged).

- `TestTickReportsAPRWithMoreChecksThanItReads`: `hasNextPage` on contexts: stderr names it, no prompt, memory unchanged.
- `TestTickDryRunNamesTheCIForwardWithoutSendingIt`: prints the nudge line, no prompt, no cache.json.

## Tradeoffs accepted

- We accept losing the idle-In-Review escalation for an ignored CI failure (today: two repeats then Needs Human) in exchange for exactly one owner of "a failed check" and one message per run. In Progress still has the stall clock; In Review relies on the worker acting on a direct instruction.
- We accept one `gh` call per live worker per tick (working workers included, In Progress PRs that may not exist yet) in exchange for mid-turn delivery and In Progress coverage. Reads stay sequential and bounded by `PRTimeout` each.
- We accept forwarding on first sighting (a deleted cache repeats one message per red PR) in exchange for never losing a failure silently.
- We accept stale keys of re-run runs sitting in `CIForwarded` until the head moves, in exchange for never re-forwarding a run that GitHub transiently omits.
- We accept a one-time test churn: the PR-nudge tests that use `checks: "FAILURE"` as the generic needs-work fixture move to `decision: CHANGES_REQUESTED`, and `FailedCheck`/`ErroredCheck`/`TwoProblems`/`ThreeProblems` become CI-nudge tests.

- **Extend the PR nudge** (give `inReviewIdle` run identity and let it fire for working workers and In Progress). Lost because the PR nudge is a counted escalation clock; firing it for a working worker either counts a mid-fix worker toward Needs Human or forks the counter by worker state, which is two policies under one name. Hides nothing new, exposes a rule whose meaning depends on who received it.
- **Partition: CI rule forwards new runs, PR nudge keeps "a failed check" for already-forwarded runs** (state backstop). Lost because an idle In Review worker gets three messages about one run (forward, two repeats) against "once per run", and two rules read the same fact with a hand-synced boundary between them.
- **High-water mark on `completedAt`** (clone of `CommentSeen`). One string instead of a set, but it assumes completion order equals discovery order, a legacy status only has `createdAt`, and it needs the `PendingComments` hold-back machinery so settle does not absorb an unforwarded run. The id set needs no hold-back because settle never advances it.
- **Separate `CIHead` field.** Two heads for one PR is one invariant kept in two places; `PRHead` with widened semantics derives the reset for free.

2. Do `TIMED_OUT` and `STARTUP_FAILURE` belong in the forwarded set, and is excluding `ACTION_REQUIRED`/`CANCELLED` right for your workflows?
3. UNVERIFIED GitHub facts the sketch leans on: `statusCheckRollup.contexts` is a `CheckRun | StatusContext` union with `databaseId`, `conclusion`, `detailsUrl`, `context`, `state`, `targetUrl`, `createdAt`; a re-run creates a new CheckRun id; `contexts(first:100)` with `pageInfo.hasNextPage`. These must be checked with a real `gh api graphql` before the query is finalized.
4. Is one message per tick listing all newly failing runs preferable to one per run, given a worker mid-turn?
5. Is the per-tick `gh` cost (up to `max_in_progress` + In Review count, sequential) acceptable, or should reads run concurrently in the same change?
6. Should a forward on first sighting after a deleted cache be kept, given a restart with an intact cache file forwards nothing?
7. Implementation risk: `CIForwarded []string` makes `cache.Entry` non-comparable, so settle's `c[id] == (cache.Entry{})` empty-entry check needs an `Entry.Zero()` method; is a method preferred over `reflect.DeepEqual`?

## Next implementation step

Change `pullrequest.Read` to fetch `statusCheckRollup.contexts`, parse it into `PR.FailedChecks []Check`, drop "a failed check" from `Problems`, and extend the harness `prState` with `failing []fakeCheck` so `TestTickForwardsAFailingCheckToAWorkingWorker` can be written first against `dispatch.Run`.
=== candidate 3 ===
# Forward a failing CI check to the owning worker: candidate 3

## Problem

A failing check on an In Progress or In Review ticket's PR must be typed into that ticket's worker once per failing run. Constraints from the code: `pullrequest.Read` folds checks into one rollup `state` and appends the string "a failed check" to `Problems`; it has no per-run identity. The PR nudge is count-based (`Entry.Nudges`, `nudge_limit`, escalation, reset on head change) and only for idle In Review workers. `ReadsPR` skips working/blocked workers and In Progress tickets. `prRelaunch` keys off `pr.NeedsWork()`, so a failed check also relaunches a gone In Review worker. `watch` yields one Action per ticket per tick, `Plan` stays pure, and the cache must keep its "deleting it costs at most a repeated message" contract.

**Premise check.** Premise: "the failure belongs to the PR nudge." From scratch, with per-run identity available, it would not. The PR nudge answers "is this PR in a bad state; keep asking until the head moves, then give up" (a level-triggered, counted rule). The Objective is "tell the worker about an event once" (edge-triggered, remembered by identity). Decision-log item 11 already says a new kind of event is a new forwarding rule, and the comment nudge (`CommentSeen`, at-least-once via executor-advanced mark, never escalates) is that pattern. Extending the PR nudge would make `Nudges` mean two things and give one failing check two clocks. Second premise: "the cache needs a per-ticket counter or one high-water mark." A counter can't say "this run, not that one"; a mark fails for StatusContexts, which have no id. Third: "the dispatcher already polls PRs each tick." It polls only idle In Review workers; this widens the poll, and the cost is a real consequence, not a free reuse.

Answer: CI forwarding is its own rule (`ciNudge`), it becomes the single owner of "a failed check", and the PR read returns failing runs as domain values.

## Usage (caller's view)

Worker's view: while building, a line arrives in its session:
`CI failed on PR https://github.com/o/r/pull/7 for ENG-1: lint <https://.../runs/9>; unit-tests <https://.../runs/10>. Verify each failure as your build skill's step 7 says (a flaky check gets its own ticket and a re-run, a real failure gets fixed), and push.`
It arrives once per run. A re-run that fails again is a new run and arrives again. A push that fails arrives again.

Dispatcher code (`reconcile`, the only caller):
```go
pr, _ := in.PRs[id]                         // pr.Failing []pullrequest.Check
due := prev.CIUnforwarded(pr.Head, pr.Failing) // []Check, nil on first sighting
```
Dry run prints `nudge ENG-1: CI failed`. Surface tests call `h.pr("ENG-1", prState{..., runs: ...})` then `dispatch.Run`.

## Shape

**Data.** `pullrequest.Check{Key, Name, URL}` and `PR.Failing []Check`. `Key` is opaque: `run:<databaseId>` for a CheckRun, `status:<context>@<createdAt>` for a StatusContext. A re-run gets a new databaseId (UNVERIFIED but the premise of "per run"), so identity is the run, not the check name. Failing = CheckRun conclusion FAILURE, TIMED_OUT, STARTUP_FAILURE; StatusContext FAILURE/ERROR. CANCELLED (usually superseded), ACTION_REQUIRED (needs a human), NEUTRAL, SKIPPED and pending are not failing. `Problems` no longer holds "a failed check". `Ready` still derives from the rollup state. Contexts are read with `first: 100`; a second page is an error like `maxThreads`. Wire types stay private to `Read` (per boundary-discipline).

**Cache.** `Entry.CIHead string "ci_head"` and `Entry.CIForwarded []string "ci_forwarded"`: the keys of failing runs on `CIHead` already told to the worker (or already failing at first sighting). Invariants: bounded to the failing runs of one head (settle prunes keys no longer failing, so a re-run's old run drops out); reset when a read shows a different head (a push voids old runs); NOT reset by a status change (runs belong to a head, not a status); appended only after `herdr.Prompt` succeeds. `Entry.CIUnforwarded(head, failing)` is the one pure derivation Plan and settle share: `CIHead==""` gives nil (first sighting), `CIHead!=head` gives all, else failing minus forwarded. Cache deletion cost: every run failing right then is treated as already told, so at most one missed message, never a repeat or crash. The cost-to-header text is updated.

**Message.** One prompt per tick listing every newly failing run (`name <url>; ...`, first 10 then "and N more"), not one prompt per run: three typed messages into a mid-turn session is noise, and the Objective's once-per-run is kept because each key is recorded individually. Text is fixed (`CINudge`) and keeps step 7: verify, flaky gets a ticket and re-run, real gets fixed. Nudges carry no source tag, as today.

**Policy.** Working and Idle workers get it (like the comment nudge; the prompt lands mid-turn). Blocked workers get nothing and nothing is recorded (text would land in the question dialog), so it fires once unblocked. Never counts toward `nudge_limit`, never escalates. `ciNudge` runs in `watch` after `commentNudge`, before the state switch, so a ticket still gets one action per tick; a PR nudge for other problems follows a later tick.

**Plan flow.** `watch`: Needs Human -> commentNudge -> **ciNudge** -> Blocked notify / Idle (inReviewIdle or stall). `ReadsPR` widens to In Progress and In Review, worker Working, Idle or (In Review only) None; Blocked skipped. `prRelaunch` gains `t.Status == InReview` (PRs now holds In Progress PRs, which must never relaunch via the PR path) and fires on `pr.NeedsWork() || len(CIUnforwarded) > 0`, preserving today's "failed check relaunches a gone In Review worker"; the relaunch Reason keeps the phrase "a failed check". After relaunch the idle worker gets the CI nudge. Relaunches still count against `nudge_limit` per head.

**Executor/settle.** Executor Nudge success: `ReasonComment` advances `CommentSeen`; `ReasonCI` appends `a.CIKeys` to `CIForwarded` and touches neither `Nudges` nor `ResumePending`; else unchanged. Settle: the existing head logic (`Nudges`, `Relaunches`, `PRHead`) is guarded to In Review, since an In Progress PR would otherwise reset stall `Nudges` through `NudgesAt`. New `settleCI(pr)`: baseline on `CIHead==""`, reset on head change, else prune. An unread PR changes nothing. Absent-ticket section keeps `CIHead`/`CIForwarded` while the ticket holds a lease, mirroring `CommentSeen`, so a paused-then-resumed worker hears about a failure that landed while paused.

**Depth.** The caller surface is one field (`pr.Failing`) and one method (`CIUnforwarded`); GitHub's union types, conclusion mapping, pagination, baseline, push reset and pruning hide behind them. One owner for "a failed check": `Failing`/`ciNudge`; the PR nudge no longer sees it.

**Failure cases.**

| Case | Remembered |
|---|---|
| Prompt refused/errors | nothing; keys not appended; same text next tick |
| Worker Blocked | nothing; no read; fires after unblock |
| PR read failed | nothing changes; ticket skipped like today |
| Push (head moves) | CIHead=new, CIForwarded=nil; new failing runs forward |
| Re-run of same check | new key; old pruned; failing again forwards again |
| Cache deleted | first read baselines current failures: one missed message at most |
| Worker gone, relaunched | entry kept (same ticket present); relaunch then idle worker gets nudge |
| Ticket leaves, re-enters | kept only while it holds a lease; otherwise baseline |
| Crash after prompt, before save | key unrecorded; one repeated message |

**Tests (through `dispatch.Run`, `review_test.go` helpers extended with `runs []run` in `prState`, failing a CheckRun with id/name/conclusion/url).**
- `TestTickForwardsANewFailingRunToAnIdleWorkerOnce`: tick twice; one prompt with name and URL, second tick silent.
- `TestTickForwardsToAWorkingInProgressWorker`: In Progress, working, PR read, prompt sent.
- `TestTickListsEveryNewlyFailingRunInOnePrompt`.
- `TestTickRecordsButDoesNotForwardARunFailingAtFirstSighting` (fresh cache).
- `TestTickForwardsAgainWhenAFailedRunIsRerunAndFailsAgain` and `...WhenAPushFailsToo`.
- `TestTickDoesNotForwardCancelledOrActionRequiredRuns`, `...StatusContextFailureIsForwarded`.
- `TestTickRetriesARefusedCIPrompt` (herdr refuses once, delivered next tick).
- `TestTickHoldsCIForwardWhileBlockedThenSendsAfterUnblock`, and does not read the PR then.
- `TestTickCINudgeNeverCountsTowardNudgeLimitOrEscalates`.
- `TestTickRelaunchesAGoneInReviewWorkerForAFailedCheckThenForwardsIt`.
- `TestTickDoesNotRelaunchAnInProgressWorkerForAFailedCheck`.
- `TestTickKeepsStallNudgeCountWhenAnInProgressPRIsRead` (guards the settle bug).
- `TestTickLeavesCIKeysForAPausedTicketWithALease`.
- `TestTickReportsAPRWithMoreChecksThanItReads`; `TestTickDryRunNamesTheCINudgeWithoutSendingIt`.
- Existing tests updated: FailedCheck/ErroredCheck rows in the PR-problem table become CI-nudge tests; "escalates after two PR nudges" re-keyed to a merge conflict; `DoesNotReadThePRWhileTheInReviewWorkerIsBusy` now asserts a read for Working and none for Blocked.

## Tradeoffs accepted

- We accept that a failing check no longer escalates to Needs Human in exchange for one owner and no double clock; a worker that ignores the message leaves the ticket quiet. The old behavior is level-triggered, the Objective is edge-triggered.
- We accept one extra gh call per non-blocked In Progress/In Review ticket per tick in exchange for catching failures while a worker is busy. In Progress tickets with no PR yet cost an empty call.
- We accept a missed message after cache deletion (baseline) in exchange for never replaying old failures on restart.
- We accept batching runs into one prompt over one prompt per run.
- A cancelled-only red rollup is not forwarded; the PR just isn't Ready.

## Alternatives considered

- Extend the PR nudge with check names: keeps `Nudges` count semantics, so the same failing run repeats then escalates; two meanings in one counter and no In Progress coverage. Shallow: callers of `Problems` would need run identity anyway.
- High-water mark like `CommentSeen`: simplest cache, but StatusContexts have no id and run ids are not guaranteed ordered; rejected.
- Per-ticket "last forwarded head" only: forwards once per head, misses a second failing check on the same head and re-runs; fails "once per failing run".
- Store every key ever seen: unbounded; rejected for the head-scoped, pruned set.

## Open questions and risks

- Should a failing check that the worker never addresses ever escalate (say, after N idle ticks past the forward)? I chose no.
- Is the GitHub shape right: new CheckRun id per re-run, `contexts` union fields, CANCELLED conclusion handling? None verified against live GitHub; needs a recorded real response in a fixture.
- Is the extra polling cost acceptable for large In Review queues, and should In Progress reads wait until the branch has a pushed ref?
- A PR first read while already red (dispatcher started late) is never forwarded; is that acceptable?
- Docs to update: guide "Nudges and notifications"/"In Review", config `nudge_limit`, blueprint criterion 9, Nudges, cache and Scale sections, decision-log item 11.

## Next implementation step

Extend `pullrequest.Read` with the `contexts` query and `PR.Failing`, with a surface test that reads a failing CheckRun through `dispatch.Run`.

Phase A (grounding) and Phase B (the three-candidate sketch) are done, and I stopped there as you asked. Nothing was run against GitHub, and the sketches are not compiled. I did not touch Linear, write the blueprint, size or file a ticket, or return the tree.

Files are in the repo root:
- `scratch/grounding.md`
- `evidence.md` (grounding, then each candidate's rationale)
- `artifact.md` (the synthesized design package)
- `note.md` (the synthesis note)

## Contract sketch

**Decision: its own rule, not an extension of the PR nudge.**
- All three candidates reached this independently, and each tested the premise that the failure belongs to the PR nudge.
- The PR nudge is a counted reminder that escalates, and it only reaches an idle In Review worker. A failing run is a one-time event.
- "A failed check" leaves `PR.Problems`, so one rule owns it. The PR nudge then covers only changes requested, unresolved threads and merge conflicts, and `nudge_limit` counts those review rounds only.

**What the cache remembers:** one new field per ticket, `ci: {head, told[], idle}`.
- `told` holds the keys of the runs this ticket's current worker was told about on the current PR head. A key is `run:<databaseId>` for a check run, or `status:<context>@<createdAt>` for an old-style status. A re-run is a new run, so it gets a new key.
- `told` is cleared when the head moves, when a worker is launched, and when the ticket escalates. It is not trimmed just because a key is missing from one read. That is bounded by the runs on one head.
- `idle` counts idle ticks with a told run still failing, for the backstop below.
- A refused prompt, a blocked worker or a failed PR read records nothing, so the forward is retried.
- If the cache is deleted, every red run is forwarded once more. Recording first sightings without forwarding, as the comment nudge does, would leave a red PR silent forever after cache loss.

**Surface a test binds to:**
- **PR read:** it returns `PR.Failing []Check{Key, Name, Conclusion, URL}` and `ChecksRunning`.
- **Which runs count:** `FAILURE`, `TIMED_OUT` and `STARTUP_FAILURE` check runs, and `FAILURE` or `ERROR` statuses. Cancelled and action-required runs are not forwarded.
- **Who gets it:** In Progress or In Review, worker Working or Idle, never Blocked; design tickets are never read. It runs right after the comment nudge, one Action per ticket per tick.
- **Message:** one per tick, listing every newly failing run. The text is fixed: `PR <url> for <ticket> has <n failed check(s)>: <name> (<conclusion>) <url>; …. Handle it as your build skill's step 7 says.` I dropped "and push" so a flaky check still gets a re-run.
- **Output lines:** the dry run prints `nudge ENG-1: check failed`. A relaunch for a red check still prints `launch ENG-1: PR needs work: a failed check: ok`.
- **Limits:** the forward never counts toward `nudge_limit` and never escalates by itself.

**What was considered:**
- Candidate 1 (opus) is the base.
- From candidate 2 I took the no-trim rule and the narrower list of failing conclusions.
- A read-only opus judge found that candidate 1's backstop would escalate on the first idle tick, which can fire too early. I changed it to wait `nudge_limit` idle ticks.
- Candidate 2 can end up stuck: a relaunched worker is told, exits without pushing, and is neither relaunched nor escalated. I rejected that design.
- Candidate 3 records already-failing runs on first sighting without forwarding them. I rejected that for the cache-loss reason above.
- I also rejected a high-water mark, because run ids order by start rather than finish and statuses have no id. I rejected one message per run as too slow and noisy.

## What you must decide next

1. **Approve or push back on the contract sketch above.** If you push back on the shape, Phase A and B re-run.
2. **Backstop.** Should an idle In Review worker that ignores a forwarded failure escalate to Needs Human after `nudge_limit` idle ticks? I recommend yes. Candidates 2 and 3 had no backstop, and I consider that a silent stuck state.
3. **GitHub facts to confirm.** Nothing was checked against live GitHub, and the design depends on these, so one real `gh api graphql` capture is needed:
   - the shape of `statusCheckRollup.contexts`;
   - a new check-run id on each re-run;
   - whether the rollup keeps only the latest run per check;
   - whether a cancelled run turns the rollup red.

   The last one matters because the synthetic `rollup:<head>` check would then forward cancelled runs after all.
4. **gh cost.** The PR read now covers Working workers and In Progress tickets, including ones with no PR yet. Is one sequential call per such ticket per tick acceptable, or should an In Progress ticket skip the read until its branch is pushed?

# Phase A grounding: forwarding a failing CI check to the owning worker

Read from the repo at the current directory (Go module `github.com/kapetan-io/dispatch`). `dispatch:why` was not run: Linear and other MCPs are unavailable in this sandbox, so rationale below comes from `docs/design/decision-log.md` and `docs/design/blueprint.md` in the repo, cited by section. Anything I could not observe is marked UNVERIFIED.

## Approved Objective

When a check fails on the pull request of an In Progress or In Review ticket, the dispatcher types one message into that ticket's worker, once per failing check run, so the worker fixes it without the user relaying anything. Workers never poll GitHub. Decide whether this extends the existing pull request nudge or becomes its own rule, and what the dispatcher's cache must remember so a failure is forwarded once.

## How a tick works (dispatch.go `tick`, line 209)

One tick under a file lock: load `cache.json` -> read Linear tickets -> read herdr snapshot and `treehouse status` -> `worker.Find` per ticket -> `readPRs` -> `reconcile.Plan(input)` (pure, no side effects; also used by `--dry-run`) -> `settle(cache, ...)` -> execute actions in order -> save cache (deferred, saved even on partial failure).

Order matters and is documented at `settle` (dispatch.go:518): Plan reads LAST tick's cache; `settle` rolls counters forward BEFORE actions run; actions then add to the cache (`Nudges++`) or undo settle's advance on failure. A nudge is recorded only after `herdr.Prompt` returns nil (dispatch.go:415-426); a refused prompt (worker turned blocked after the snapshot) is not counted and retries next tick.

## The existing pull request nudge (the thing the ticket asks to extend or not)

- Data: `internal/pullrequest/pullrequest.go`. `Read` makes one `gh api graphql` call per ticket (by head branch, open PRs, newest) and returns `PR{Number, URL, Head, Problems []string, Ready bool}`. The query reads `headRefOid mergeable reviewDecision`, `commits(last:1){commit{statusCheckRollup{state}}}` and review threads. Check state is ONLY the rollup `state`: `FAILURE` or `ERROR` adds the string "a failed check" to `Problems`; any non-`SUCCESS` rollup clears `checksPassed`. The query does NOT read the individual check runs (`statusCheckRollup.contexts`), so today there is no check-run identity, name or conclusion anywhere in the code. Whether the rollup already reports FAILURE while sibling checks are still running is UNVERIFIED (no network/gh in sandbox); the design must not depend on it.
- Gate: `Input.ReadsPR` (reconcile.go:353) is true ONLY for tickets in In Review, not truncated, no children, not `design`/`design-review`, and whose worker is `None` or `Idle`. Working and blocked workers cost no call. `readPRs` (dispatch.go:607) fills `Input.PRs`; a read error goes in `PRReadFailed` and holds back only that ticket.
- Decision: `inReviewIdle` (reconcile.go:374), reached from `watch` only when `t.Status == InReview` and `w.State == Idle`. Order inside it: ready-for-review Notify (once per head via `ReadyHead`), else if `pr.NeedsWork()`: `nudges := prev.NudgesAt(status, head)`; at `NudgeLimit` (default 2, `config.NudgeLimit`) it Escalates to Needs Human; otherwise a Nudge with `Reason = "PR needs work: <problem>"` and fixed text `PRNudge = "PR %s for %s has %s. Handle it as your build skill's step 7 says, and push."`. The problem phrase joins all problems ("a failed check and a merge conflict"), so one nudge covers failed check, changes requested, unresolved thread and merge conflict together.
- Dedup today: NOT once-per-failure. It is a COUNT per (status, PR head): `Entry.Nudges` and `Entry.PRHead`; `NudgesAt` returns 0 when status or head changed (a push resets the count). So an idle worker with a failed check is nudged every tick until 2 nudges, then the ticket is escalated. There is no memory of WHICH failure was sent. A re-run of a flaky check on the same head, producing a new failure, is indistinguishable from the old one.
- A gone worker (`None`) with a PR needing work is relaunched (`prRelaunch`, reconcile.go:363), counted in `Entry.Relaunches`, same limit. The relaunched worker gets the nudge on a later tick once idle.
- `settle` (dispatch.go:565): for any ticket with a read PR, `Nudges = NudgesAt(...)`, `Relaunches = RelaunchesAt(...)`, `PRHead = pr.Head`. For a ticket NOT In Review with no read PR, `PRHead` is cleared ("the head means nothing outside In Review").

## The comment nudge: the precedent for "forward an external event once"

`decision-log.md` decision 11 (ENG-257, settled 2026-10-09): "Dispatch is the event broker. ... Each tick it polls those sources, compares what it finds with its cache, and forwards what the receiver doesn't know yet, as a nudge to a worker or a notification to you. Workers never poll. A new kind of event is a new forwarding rule in the dispatcher, never an instruction for workers to check something themselves." The comment nudge "is one such rule, like the PR nudge."

Its mechanics (reconcile.go:339 `commentNudge`, :309 `CommentDue`, :318 `PendingComments`, dispatch.go:543 and :420):
- Watermark in cache: `Entry.CommentSeen` = creation time of newest comment accounted for; `""` = never seen (first sighting records without nudging, so restarting nudges nobody for old events); `"0"` = seen, none.
- Fires for a WORKING or IDLE worker (typing into a busy Claude session delivers mid-turn), In Progress or In Review. Skips a blocked worker (the text would land in its question dialog) and `design-review`.
- Does NOT count toward `Nudges`/`NudgeLimit` and never escalates (the dispatch loop only does `e.Nudges++` when `Reason != ReasonComment`).
- Watermark advances in `settle` unless `PendingComments` says a nudge is owed or the worker is blocked or in an unread repo; on a successful nudge the executor sets it. So a nudge that failed or was skipped is retried; a comment dropped for another reason (a resume nudge stands in) is absorbed.
- It takes priority in `watch` over stall/PR nudges, which fire on a later tick (one Action per ticket per tick).
- Explicitly NOT retried: a comment that arrives while the worker is gone is not nudged later.

## Cache contract (internal/cache/cache.go)

# Rationale: candidate 1, the check forward as its own rule with a told-set

## Problem

A check that fails on the PR of an In Progress or In Review ticket should reach that ticket's worker once, typed in by the dispatcher (decision 11: workers never poll). The existing machinery makes the shape non-obvious in three ways:

- The PR nudge already says "a failed check". But it reads only the rollup `state`, and only for idle or gone In Review workers. It also counts toward `NudgeLimit` and escalates. The forward needs none of that.
- The cache must stay comparable (`Entry == Entry{}`). Losing the cache may repeat at most one message.
- `PRHead`, `Nudges` and `NudgesAt` carry In Review semantics that escalation and four tests rely on.

The window that matters most is In Progress with a working worker: the PR has just opened and CI fails for the first time. Today that window has no PR read at all.

## Usage (caller's view)

The worker receives `On PR <url> for ENG-1, check test (<details url>) failed. Handle what failed as your build skill's step 7 says.` exactly once per failed run. A dry run prints `nudge ENG-1: check failed`. `watch` calls `in.checkNudge(t, w, prev)` right after `commentNudge`. The executor's one new line is `case ReasonCheck: e.ChecksTold = a.Checks`. See design.md for the full sketch.

## Shape

- **Separate rule, shared read.** `checkNudge` sits beside `commentNudge` and follows its policy. It forwards to working or idle workers, never blocked ones, and never counts or escalates. The PR nudge is unchanged and remains the backstop for an idle worker that doesn't act. (Per decision 11, and per two-ways-to-do-one-task: a failure has one forwarding rule. The PR nudge is a nag about a condition, not a forward.)
- **Identity lives in `pullrequest`.** The GraphQL `CheckRun` and `StatusContext` are parsed into a domain `Failure{Key, Name, URL}` behind `Read`. Nothing outside the package sees `databaseId`, `conclusion` or `__typename`. The key is opaque and includes the completion time, so the rule is right whether a re-run creates a new id or reuses the old one. (Per boundary-discipline.)
- **The cache stores a set, not a watermark.** Ids follow creation order and failures arrive in completion order, so an id watermark loses failures and a time watermark loses ties. `cache.Told` is a typed comma-joined string. It keeps `Entry` comparable, and only its own methods parse it. (Per encode-lessons-in-structure.)
- **One writer, idempotent.** Only the executor writes `ChecksTold`, after `herdr.Prompt` returns nil. It assigns the complete current set computed by the pure `Plan`. It never appends. So a crash, a refused prompt or a repeated tick sends at most what is still owed. `settle` never touches the field, so there is no "pending" helper like `PendingComments` to keep in step with it. (Per make-operations-idempotent and single source of truth.)
- **What it deliberately does not do.** It reads only the head commit, so failures on old heads are never forwarded. It ignores CANCELLED. It keeps nothing for an absent ticket. It does not reset on a status change, because keys are global. It does not change `PRHead`, `Nudges` or escalation.

Interface depth: callers see one method, one constant, one `Action` field and one cache field. GraphQL union parsing, key building, the set's encoding and pruning all stay behind `pullrequest.Read` and `cache.Told`.

## Tradeoffs accepted

- We accept more `gh` calls in exchange for reaching the In Progress window: one call per tick for each live, non-blocked In Progress or In Review worker. That is a few calls every 5 minutes, and `PRTimeout` bounds each one. No "PR exists" hint is cached, because a hint would be a second copy of GitHub's truth.
- We accept that an idle In Review worker may hear about one failure twice in exchange for keeping the PR nudge untouched: first the specific forward, then the generic PR nudge "a failed check" on a later tick if it is still idle. The second message is the nag that leads to escalation, and that is intended.
- We accept repeating one message after the cache is deleted, or after a ticket leaves and returns, in exchange for never losing a failure. This differs on purpose from the comment nudge, which records the first sighting without nudging, because a failing CI left unforwarded blocks a merge.
- We accept that a working worker gets the text mid-turn, as the comment nudge already does.

## Alternatives considered

- **Extend the PR nudge** by adding "a failed check" forwarding to `inReviewIdle`. It lost because it can't reach working workers or In Progress tickets without changing what `Nudges` and `PRHead` mean. It would also expose counted and uncounted sends through one counter. It hides less and leaks more.
- **Watermark** (`CheckSeen int64` max `databaseId`, or the RFC 3339 `completedAt` of the newest failure, like `CommentSeen`). It is simpler, but the id version loses failures that complete out of creation order, and the time version loses failures that complete in the same second. Both break "once per run".
- **Digest of the failing set** (`sha(head+keys)`), forwarded whenever it changes. It can't tell which failure is new, so it repeats old failures whenever a new one appears or an old one clears.

## Open questions and risks

- Does `statusCheckRollup.contexts` list every run on the commit or only the latest per check, and does a GitHub Actions re-run get a new `databaseId`? (UNVERIFIED. The key covers both.)
- Is 100 contexts per page enough, or should overflow forward the first page instead of failing the read?
- Should `ACTION_REQUIRED` count as a failure?
- Should a forward to an idle In Review worker push back that tick's PR nudge by one tick, as designed, or replace the first PR nudge?
- In the In Progress window, is reading every tick for working workers acceptable once `max_in_progress` grows?

Extend `pullrequest.Read` and the fake `gh` fixture with `contexts` → `Failures`, and get a `pullrequest` table test green before touching `reconcile`.

From scratch with today's signals, the PR nudge's three properties (idle-only, In Review-only, counted-and-escalating) are each the opposite of what the objective asks (In Progress too, once per run, no escalation), and it is state-based ("the PR has problems") where this is event-based ("this run failed"). The comment nudge is the precedent for an event with a watermark. Second premise: "once per failing check run" needs a run identity. GitHub gives `CheckRun.completedAt`/`databaseId` and `StatusContext.createdAt`; I key on the time because it moves whether a re-run mints a new id or reuses one (UNVERIFIED which), and a time is one comparable string.

## Usage (caller's view)

See design.md: silent config-free behavior; one `nudge ENG-x: CI failed` line per new failure; `ci_failed_seen` in the cache.

## Shape

Own rule `ciNudge`, modeled on `commentNudge`: a single watermark string `CIFailSeen`, advanced only by the executor after `herdr.Prompt` succeeds, never by `settle`. Working and idle workers receive it (mid-turn delivery, as comments do); blocked and gone workers do not, and since the watermark does not move they are told later or via the existing relaunch. It does not count toward `NudgeLimit`. The module hides: failure classification (conclusions and states), identity, dedupe and the retry rule, behind `PR.FailedAfter(seen)` and `ciNudge`; callers see one Action kind they already know. Ownership: CI failure is owned by exactly one rule, so "a failed check" leaves `Problems`; this avoids two ways to do one task (the PR nudge and CI nudge both typing for the same red check). `prRelaunch` keeps relaunching on `CIFailed()`. The `settle` PR block is scoped to In Review so the new In Progress read cannot corrupt stall counts or `PRHead` (single source of truth for head semantics). Watermark compares GitHub timestamps to GitHub timestamps, so no local clock, and per make-operations-idempotent a crash between prompt and save repeats at most one message.

## Synthesis decision

(Filled in by the orchestrator.)

## Tradeoffs accepted

- We accept second-granularity ties (a second failure with the same `completedAt` as the watermark, appearing after our read, is missed) in exchange for a single comparable string and no per-run list.
- We accept no repeat and no escalation for a worker that ignores a CI failure, in exchange for strict once-per-run; a still-red PR is not re-nudged until a new run fails. The user sees it on the PR.
- We accept an extra `gh` call per tick per working In Progress/In Review ticket with a branch, in exchange for catching failures mid-turn; idle-only reads would defeat the objective.
- We accept rewriting existing PR-nudge tests that assert the "failed check" phrase, since that behavior moves to the new rule.

## Alternatives considered

- Extend the PR nudge with a per-head failed-check list: shallow and leaky. It exposes counts, heads and run lists to the same escalation path, needs a slice in `Entry` (breaking `==`), and still can't reach working or In Progress workers.
- Store a set of forwarded run ids (`[]string`/map): exact, but breaks `Entry == Entry{}`, grows unboundedly, and needs pruning; the watermark gives the same dedupe because a later run always completes later. Kept as the documented fallback.
- Reset-on-head like `Nudges`: forwards a stale failure again after an unrelated push and can't tell a re-run on the same head. Lost.

## Open questions and risks

- Does a GitHub Actions re-run advance `completedAt` on the check run (or create a new run)? If not, is the `name@completedAt@databaseId` fallback acceptable?
- Should a CI failure on a PR the worker already knows about (it is mid-fix, working) be suppressed, or is a mid-turn message always fine?
- Is one extra graphql call per working worker per tick within the `PRTimeout`/lock budget at the expected ticket count?
- Should an ignored red PR eventually escalate, accepting a second rule's counter?

## Next implementation step

Extend `pullrequest.Read`'s query and parse `FailedChecks` with a fixture-driven unit test, then add `ciNudge` and the three-way executor case.

```
On PR <url> for ENG-1, check test (<job url>) failed. Handle what failed as your build skill's step 7 says.
```

When several fail in the same tick, the message names them all (`checks lint (url) and test (url) failed`).

**What the user sees.**
- `dispatch tick --dry-run` prints `nudge ENG-1: check failed`, sends nothing and writes nothing.
- `cache.json` gains `"checks_told"`, a string of failure keys joined by newlines.

**What the cache remembers.** It remembers the set of failures already told, not a time watermark. A watermark loses two failures that finish in the same second, and it loses a run that a third-party CI reports late with an older time.
- Each failure has a key: `run:<databaseId>@<completedAt>` for a check run, `status:<context>@<createdAt>` for a commit status.
- The field is written only after the prompt lands, and it never touches `Nudges` or `PRHead`.
- It is kept while the ticket holds a lease. A deleted cache repeats at most one message.

**What changes in the code.**
- The PR read now fetches each check run, not just the rollup state.
- It is read for In Progress tickets and for working workers, never for a blocked one.
- `checkNudge` runs after the comment nudge and never counts toward the nudge limit or escalates.
- The PR nudge is untouched and stays as the backstop, so an idle In Review worker can hear about a failure twice.

- **Comma bug:** the judge found that the base candidate joined keys with commas. A status name like `ci/test (linux, go1.22)` would never match and repeat every tick, so keys are now newline-joined.
- **More than 100 checks:** that case forwards what is visible and logs to stderr, instead of failing the PR read.
- **From the other candidates:** I took the `t.Branch != ""` gate, the lease carve-out for the cache field, and the backstop tests.
- **Rejected:** removing "a failed check" from the PR nudge, which would lose the escalation after two idle nudges.

1. **Approve the contract sketch.** Say if you want a different shape, and I'll re-ground and re-sketch.

Repo: kapetan-io/dispatch (Go). No docs/adr/ and no CONTEXT.md exist. Design intent lives in docs/design/blueprint.md and docs/design/decision-log.md. Nothing below was run against live GitHub; it is traced from code and the blueprint.

- `Plan(in Input) []Action` is pure. It reads Linear tickets, a herdr/treehouse worker lookup (`worker.State` = none|working|idle|blocked), PRs read from GitHub, and last tick's `cache.Cache`. The executor in dispatch.go (`switch a.Kind`) performs actions, then mutates the cache. `settle()` rolls the cache forward BEFORE actions run, and failed actions undo their counter changes (a refused nudge "is not counted").
- Per-ticket decisions live in `Input.watch(t)`. Order: Needs Human notify; skip non-In Progress/In Review; `commentNudge`; blocked notify; idle -> In Review goes to `inReviewIdle`, In Progress gets stall/resume nudge. One action per ticket per tick: "A comment nudge replaces any other nudge for that tick".
- Design and design-review tickets, tickets with children, and tickets with truncated labels are never nudged.

## The existing PR nudge (the thing to extend or not)
- `internal/pullrequest.Read` makes ONE `gh api graphql` call per ticket. It returns `PR{Number, URL, Head, Problems []string, Ready bool}`. Check state comes only from `commits(last:1).statusCheckRollup.state`: FAILURE or ERROR adds the problem string "a failed check". PENDING/EXPECTED are neither failure nor ready. There is NO per-check data: no check run id, name, conclusion or log URL. So today the dispatcher cannot say which check failed, nor tell two failures on one head apart.
- Problems also include "changes requested", "an unresolved review thread", "a merge conflict". All are joined into one phrase.
- `ReadsPR(t)` is true only for status In Review, not design/design-review/children/truncated, and worker state none or idle. Working and blocked workers cost no call. In Progress tickets are never read. This is a cost decision: "one gh api graphql call per In Review ticket whose worker is idle or gone".
- `inReviewIdle`: ready PR -> notify once per head (`ReadyHead`); else if NeedsWork -> `nudges := prev.NudgesAt(status, head)`; if >= NudgeLimit (config default 2) -> Escalate to Needs Human ("stayed idle through N nudges about <url> without pushing"); else Nudge with fixed text `PRNudge = "PR %s for %s has %s. Handle it as your build skill's step 7 says, and push."`. The nudge repeats each tick until nudge limit, i.e. it fires on STATE ("PR currently has a failure"), not on an EVENT.
- A worker that is gone while the PR needs work is relaunched (`prRelaunch`, counted by `Relaunches`, same limit, not counted against the worker cap).
- Nudge text is fixed because "the build-worker skill and the tests rely on the exact wording". skills/build/SKILL.md step 7 says: real failure gets fixed; flaky check gets its own Backlog ticket and a re-run. Step 1: "A ticket already In Review has its PR open, so skip to step 7." Blueprint invariant: "The worker runs no /loop, cron or babysit-pr polling. A nudge is its only wake-up." Blueprint rule: dispatcher "only nudges with fixed text".

## The cache (internal/cache/cache.go)
Per-ticket `Entry` persisted as JSON, atomically saved. Deleting it "loses little" by design (counters reset, a notification may repeat, first sighting of comments nudges nobody). Relevant fields:
- `Nudges` counts nudges (resume included) since last status change; reset when status changes or, for In Review, when `PRHead` moves (`NudgesAt`).
- `PRHead`: head SHA when last read. Cleared when the ticket leaves In Review ("a stale one would hide a push later"). Only updated when the PR was read this tick (`prs[id]` present).

`herdr.Prompt(ctx, bin, paneID, text)` types into the pane; it refuses a blocked worker. - Dispatcher is stateless-ish: Linear is the record; cache is disposable. A design needing a durable cache is a departure.
- Cost: one Linear query + one gh call per In Review ticket with idle/gone worker per tick (interval default 5 min, blueprint "A tick costs..."). Extending reads to In Progress tickets (including working workers) widens that cost. In Progress tickets usually have no PR yet.
- Workers never poll GitHub (ticket Objective; blueprint invariant 6).

1. "Once per failing check run" needs a per-check identity. Rollup state gives none; the GraphQL query must grow (statusCheckRollup.contexts nodes: CheckRun {databaseId, name, conclusion, detailsUrl} and StatusContext {context, state}). A re-run of a check on the same head makes a NEW check run (new id), so (head,name) is not the same key as run id. A legacy commit status (StatusContext) has no run id; its identity would be (context, state, targetUrl or createdAt).
2. The existing PR nudge is state-triggered and capped; the new behavior is event-triggered, once per run, uncapped by Nudges, and should reach a WORKING worker and an In Progress ticket too. 3. If both fire, the same failing check would be reported twice (check-failure nudge, then "PR has a failed check" PR nudge on a later tick) and the PR nudge counts toward escalation. Any shape must say how "a failed check" interacts with the existing PR nudge.
4. A failure that arrives while the worker is blocked must not be marked forwarded (the comment path holds its marker back for this reason).
5. Failed `herdr.Prompt` must not mark the run forwarded; a successful one must record it before the next tick can re-plan it. Plan is pure and runs before actions, so "forwarded" can only be written by the executor.
6. Cache pruning drops entries when the ticket is paused/finished; a run id that is forgotten while the PR is still open would be re-forwarded on return.
7. Tests: surface tests drive Plan/tick with fake gh, herdr, linear (see nudge_test.go, dispatch_test.go, review_test.go). Fixed text is asserted exactly.

The CI-failure forwarding should be its own rule next to the comment nudge, not an extension of the existing PR nudge. It's a design only. I haven't built or compiled anything, and nothing has been checked against live GitHub.

## Contract sketch (needs your approval)

- **Message.** Text like `Checks failed on PR <url> for <ticket>: test (<run url>). Read each failure's log, handle it as your build skill's step 7 says, and push.` goes to a working or idle worker on an In Progress or In Review ticket.
- **When it fires.** Once per check run, not per commit. A re-run of a flaky check on the same commit counts as a new run and is forwarded again if it fails. The build skill tells workers to re-run flaky checks, so a per-commit marker would swallow that failure.
- **Cache.** One new field per ticket, `forwarded_checks`: the ids of failed runs already typed into the worker. It holds nothing pending.
  - **When it's written.** Only after the message lands.
  - **When it's pruned.** To the runs still failing whenever the PR is read.
  - **If the cache is deleted.** Each still-failing run is forwarded once more.
  - **Why no pending state.** A failing check stays visible on GitHub, so "owed" is just failing minus forwarded. A blocked worker, a failed send or a GitHub error all retry on the next tick with no extra bookkeeping.
- **GitHub read.** The same single query now returns each failed check's id, name and URL. It no longer returns only the aggregate state.
- **Existing nudges.** The forward doesn't count toward `NudgeLimit`. The PR nudge and the stall nudge stay as backstops, so a worker that ignores the forward still escalates to Needs Human.
- **Who gets it.** Blocked workers wait until unblocked. A gone worker is launched or relaunched as today, then gets the forward.
- **One guard.** A push seen on an In Progress ticket must not reset its stall count, so the head tracking stays limited to In Review.

## Why not the alternatives

I considered extending the PR nudge, keying by commit and a comment-style timestamp watermark. Three independent candidates, with a cross-judge, all converged on a separate rule keyed by run. Extending the PR nudge can't reach working or In Progress workers without changing a counted rule. Keying by commit swallows re-runs, and a watermark depends on CI apps' clocks.

## What you must decide next

1. **Approve or push back on the contract sketch above.** If you push back on the shape, I re-ground and re-run the sketches.
2. **Batching.** Several new failures in one tick go out as one message listing all of them. Is that "one message per failing check run", or do you want one prompt per run?
3. **Cancelled runs.** I excluded cancelled runs, because concurrency groups cancel superseded runs on every push. Do you agree?
4. **In Progress cost.** Reading every working In Progress worker's PR each tick costs about one extra GitHub call per ticket, and most have no PR yet. Do you accept that, or want a cheaper gate such as reading only after the first push?
5. **Check on a live PR.** Two GitHub behaviors are assumed from the code, not observed: a re-run gets a new run id, and the check list shows only the latest run of each check. Should I check them on a live PR before the build?

## Files

`artifact.md` is the design package and `note.md` is the synthesis note. `evidence.md` joins the grounding and the three candidates' rationale files.

I stopped here, as you asked. I did not size the work, file a ticket, or write the blueprint to Linear.

When a check fails on the pull request of an In Progress or In Review ticket, the dispatcher types one message into that ticket's worker, once per failing check run, so the worker fixes it without the user relaying anything. Cache is saved after the tick (cache.Save, atomic rename).

`Read(ctx, bin, repoDir, branch, timeout)`: ONE `gh api graphql` call per ticket, finds the newest OPEN PR with headRefName == ticket branch. Query fetches `number url headRefOid mergeable reviewDecision commits(last:1){commit{statusCheckRollup{state}}} reviewThreads(first:100)`. Only the ROLLUP `state` is read (FAILURE/ERROR => Problems gets "a failed check"; any state != SUCCESS => not "checksPassed"). There is NO per-check identity today: no check run id, name, conclusion, URL. PR struct = {Number, URL, Head, Problems []string, Ready bool}. `NeedsWork()` = len(Problems)>0, used by (a) the PR nudge, (b) `prRelaunch` (In Review, worker None, NeedsWork => relaunch a worker), (c) `Ready` (= !NeedsWork && checksPassed && MERGEABLE, drives the ready-for-review notification once per head via cache ReadyHead). `Input.ReadsPR(t)` (reconcile.go ~line 281): true only for status == InReview, not LabelsTruncated, no children, no `design`/`design-review` label, and worker State is None or Idle. So today: In Progress tickets never have their PR read; a Working or Blocked In Review worker's PR is not read (saves a gh call). Handle it as your build skill's step 7 says, and push."` where %s is `pr.Problem()` e.g. "a failed check and a merge conflict". Notice this already tells an idle In Review worker about "a failed check" with no check identity, may repeat up to the limit per head, and there is no run-level dedupe. A new rule must coexist with it or replace its failed-check part, or an idle worker gets two messages for one failure. Also `Ready`/relaunch depend on the rollup "FAILURE" so removing the failed-check Problem from PR.Problems changes those too.

Not-nudged cases (worker gone, resume pending, design-review) are absorbed, never replayed. ## Cache (internal/cache/cache.go)
JSON file, map[ticket id]Entry, atomic write, corrupt file = empty cache. Entry fields listed above plus LastStatus, LaunchFailures, ResumePending, NotifyPending, BlockedTicks, PendingComment/TicketID, TeardownWarned. Anything new must be `omitempty` so old caches load. `Plan` only READS the cache; `settle` and the action loop write it.

internal/worker: ticket id -> treehouse lease -> herdr workspace -> claude agent, State None|Working|Idle|Blocked. `herdr.Prompt(ctx, bin, pane, text)` types text and submits it, refusing a blocked agent. `tell.go` is the manual `dispatch tell <ticket> <text>` version.

5. Cache growth: a long-lived ticket accumulates run ids unless pruned (PRHead resets on push, so ids can be scoped per head).

- The PR is read only for In Review tickets with an idle or absent worker.

(Filled in later.)

- We accept one repeated message per ticket after cache deletion in exchange for never silently dropping a failure. The comment rule drops instead; for a red PR a drop leaves nobody informed, which is worse than one extra line. There is no "first sighting" special case.
- We accept no escalation to Needs Human for a worker that ignores a forwarded failure in exchange for "once per run". The failed-check part of the counted PR nudge was the backstop; when runs are identified it is gone. A user still sees the red PR and the idle workspace.
- We accept one more GraphQL call per In Progress and Working ticket per tick in exchange for catching failures where they happen. Blocked tickets and In Progress tickets without a worker are skipped.
- We accept one message per ticket per tick covering all due runs rather than one message per run: "once per run" holds (each id is in exactly one message), and it matches the one-action-per-ticket shape of `watch` and avoids typing several lines into a Working agent.
- We accept at-least-once across a crash between `Prompt` and `Save`, like every other nudge.
- We accept that the same failure is told again when the worker was relaunched, since the new worker is the one that must learn it. This may look redundant to a reader; it is the "gone worker" rule.
- The fallback inside `NudgeProblem` can look like two ways to do one task. It exists only for a red rollup with no nameable run, and removing it would turn a read gap into silence.

## Alternatives considered

- Extend the PR nudge with a per-run dedupe. Loses on depth: one function with a counted state rule and an event rule, two different resets (push vs per-run), and it still would not reach Working workers or In Progress tickets without further changes to `inReviewIdle`.

- Record seen ids in Linear (a comment per failure) so the cache is not needed. Loses on blueprint: the dispatcher never comments to record a nudge, and it adds noise on the ticket.
- Count per-(head, check name) instead of per run id. Loses the objective: a re-run that fails again is a new failure a worker must hear about.
- Keep everything, drop the failed-check part of the PR nudge entirely. Simplest, rejected because a red rollup with unidentified runs would go unannounced.

- Do the check-run GraphQL fields (`databaseId`, `name`, `conclusion`, `StatusContext.context/state/createdAt`, `contexts(first:)`) exist as written? All are UNVERIFIED; a real `gh api graphql` smoke is the first thing to run.

- Should a worker that stays idle after a forwarded failure eventually escalate? Not decided here; it would need a separate count and a user decision on the limit.
- Is a contexts list over 100 entries realistic for this repo? The design errors on it like review threads; the user may prefer paging.
- Should CANCELLED and ACTION_REQUIRED runs ever be forwarded? Chosen: no.

I did not discuss, size, file a ticket, write a blueprint or return the tree, as you asked. Nothing was run or tested, because the sandbox has no network. Every GitHub GraphQL name below is written from memory and unverified.

## Contract sketch

This is its own rule, the **check nudge**, beside the comment nudge. The existing pull request nudge keeps its wording and its limit of two nudges. It counts, escalates, and only reaches an idle In Review worker. That makes it a watchdog, not a once-per-failure message, so it can't carry this feature.

**Message.** One message goes to a working or idle worker. It takes the tick after the comment nudge and ahead of the stall, resume and pull request nudges. It never counts toward the nudge limit:
```
Check "go test" (<log url>) failed on PR <url> for ENG-1. Handle it as your build skill's step 7 says, and push.
```
Several runs failing in one tick go in one message that names them all. The dry-run line is `nudge ENG-1: failed check: go test`.

**What the pull request read adds.** `PR.Failures` is a list of `{ID, Name, URL}`, one per failed check run. It comes from `statusCheckRollup.contexts` in the same single `gh` call. A CheckRun counts when its conclusion is `FAILURE`, `TIMED_OUT` or `STARTUP_FAILURE`. A commit status counts when its state is `FAILURE` or `ERROR`. `Problems`, `Ready` and the relaunch rule are unchanged.

**What the cache remembers.** One new optional field, `Entry.ChecksForwarded []string`, holds the ids of failed runs already typed into the worker.
- **Written:** only the action loop adds an id, and only after `herdr.Prompt` returns nil. A refused or failed prompt records nothing, so it is retried.
- **Pruned:** settle drops ids that are no longer failing on the pull request.
- **Why a set:** a time mark could skip a run that completes late.
- **Cache loss:** deleting the cache forwards each still-failing run once more.
- **Side effect:** the `c[id] == (cache.Entry{})` check in settle must become `c[id].Empty()`, because `Entry` now holds a slice.

**When the pull request is read.** `ReadsPR` widens in two ways:
- **In Progress:** tickets with a working or idle worker.
- **In Review:** any worker that isn't blocked. A working worker is now read too, so one existing test changes: `TestTickDoesNotReadThePRWhileTheInReviewWorkerIsBusy`.

- **Extend the pull request nudge:** it only reaches an idle In Review worker, it repeats, and it escalates.
- **Completion-time marker, as `CommentSeen` does:** runs finish out of order.
- **Head-scoped set (candidates 1 and 3):** it needs a second field, and pruning already bounds the set.
- **First-sighting record (candidate 1):** it silently drops a failure that happened while the cache was missing.
- **Drop "a failed check" from the pull request nudge (candidate 3):** that removes the only escalation for a worker that ignores a forwarded failure.
- **Batched per-repo read:** it is the better design from scratch, but it is a separate change.

1. **Approve the sketch.** Or push back on the shape, which means re-grounding and re-running the sketch.

Repo: /private/tmp/e-bb0F3x/home/cwd (Go module github.com/kapetan-io/dispatch). Line numbers are from the tree at commit 21a94dc.
Subsystems traced: the PR read, the reconcile plan, the tick executor and settle step, the cache, the worker lookup, the nudge texts. Rationale: `docs/design/decision-log.md` decision 11 and `docs/design/blueprint.md`.

## Objective (approved)
When a check fails on the PR of an In Progress or In Review ticket, the dispatcher types one message into that ticket's worker, once per failing check run, so the worker fixes it without the user relaying anything. Workers never poll GitHub. Decide whether this extends the existing PR nudge or becomes its own rule, and what the dispatcher's cache must remember so a failure is forwarded once.

## Constraints that govern the design (from the repo's own decisions)
- Decision 11, "Dispatch is the event broker" (ENG-257): each tick the dispatcher polls GitHub/Linear, compares with its cache, and forwards what the receiver does not know yet. Workers never poll. "A new kind of event is a new forwarding rule in the dispatcher, never an instruction for workers to check something themselves." The comment nudge is the worked precedent: fires once per new comment, goes to a working OR idle worker (typing into a busy Claude session delivers mid-turn), skips a blocked worker until it is unblocked, counts toward neither the stall nor the PR limit, never escalates.
- Blueprint "Nudges": text is fixed, no source tag, workers treat nudges as coming from the user. The dispatcher comments on a ticket only for Needs Human or a dirty tree, never to record a nudge.
- Blueprint cache note: "Deleting the dispatcher cache loses little: counters reset and a last-seen value may repeat one notification." The cache design contract is that loss may cause at most one repeat, never a lost-forever or a storm. (cache.go package doc says the same.)

1. `tick` (dispatch.go:209) builds `reconcile.Input`: tickets, `Workers[ticket]` from `worker.Find` (ticket -> treehouse lease holder -> herdr workspace on the tree -> claude agent; state none/working/idle/blocked), cache `c`.

   - an In Progress ticket's PR is NEVER read today;
   - an In Review ticket whose worker is Working or Blocked is never read (the "costs no call" decision, blueprint Scale section: one `gh api graphql` per In Review ticket with idle/gone worker).

3. `pullrequest.Read` (internal/pullrequest/pullrequest.go) runs ONE `gh api graphql` (30-ish s timeout from `opts.PRTimeout`, `-F owner={owner}`, branch = the ticket's Linear branch name, `pullRequests(headRefName:, states: OPEN, first:1, orderBy UPDATED_AT desc)`).    - CI is read ONLY as the rollup `state`. `FAILURE` or `ERROR` adds the problem string "a failed check". Any state other than SUCCESS makes `checksPassed=false` so the PR is not Ready. PENDING and EXPECTED are "not failures" (comment: the worker has nothing to fix yet).
   - FACT with design consequence: GitHub's rollup state is PENDING while any check is still running, even when another check has already FAILED. Per-run identity needs the rollup's `contexts` connection: `CheckRun{databaseId name status conclusion detailsUrl}` and `StatusContext{context state targetUrl}` (legacy commit statuses have no databaseId, so identity there is `context` + the commit SHA, or the status `id`).
